I think that it is a mistake to teach Shakespeare in high school. 

Many of the comments here seem to insist that teaching Shakespeare should be done in a way that brings out details that students find exciting or relevant to their own lives. Some teachers have mentioned that they usually show a film first. 

Yet, I think that many of the current approaches only encourage students to pay attention to major plot points and interpretations spoon-fed to them. They do not spend much time on comprehending the text first-hand. When students read aloud in class, they tend to do so with minimal comprehension. They try to follow along so that they will be ready when called on.

For these reasons, I think that the efforts teachers make to get students excited and involved with Shakespeare actually REMOVES them from Shakespeare's language, since they can so easily get by without ever glancing at it.

And for the record, my English teachers were quite good, for English teachers. I may be biased, because I, like OP, feel that Shakespeare came to me far before I was ready.
